sources.entry: simpy - A process-based discrete-event simulation framework.

summary.name: SimPy
summary.one_liner: SimPy is a process-based discrete-event simulation framework for standard Python, where simulation processes are written as generator functions.
use_cases: model customers queuing at a checkout counter
simulate vehicles or agents moving over time
run fast-forward or real-time simulations in Python
summary.what_it_does: SimPy lets you define active components such as customers, vehicles or agents as Python generator functions that yield timeouts and events. It provides shared resource types to model limited-capacity congestion points like servers, counters and tunnels. A simulation can run as fast as possible, in real time tied to the wall clock, or be advanced one event at a time. The docs include a tutorial, topical guides, examples and an API reference. Installation is via pip and it requires Python 3.8 or later, with CPython and PyPy3 reported to work.
notable: Processes defined as plain Python generator functions
Shared resources for modeling capacity-limited congestion points
Runs as fast as possible, in real time, or stepped event by event
Ports exist in C# (SimSharp), Julia (ConcurrentSim) and R (Simmer)
caveats: Not designed for continuous simulation; it has no features specifically for that
Not needed for fixed-step simulations where processes do not interact or share resources
